title: KS3 History: KS3: Industrialisation, Empire, and Power (1750–1900)
subtitle: A condensed roadmap and revision sheet for this unit.

topics.title: 1. What powered the Industrial Revolution, and how did a Fareham ironmaster change the world?
points: **Objective:** To understand What powered the Industrial Revolution, and how did a Fareham ironmaster change the world?
**Key Topics:** Industrial Revolution, Pig Iron, Wrought Iron, Puddling Process, Rolling Mill

topics.title: 2. Was industrial work progress or punishment?
points: **Objective:** To understand Was industrial work progress or punishment?
**Key Topics:** Fareham Reds, Pug Mill, Primary Source, Historiography, Factory Acts

topics.title: 3. Did industrialisation make British towns unlivable?
points: **Objective:** To understand Did industrialisation make British towns unlivable?
**Key Topics:** Urbanisation, Laissez-faire, Miasma Theory, Provenance, Public Health

topics.title: 4. How was the British Empire built and sustained?
points: **Objective:** To understand How was the British Empire built and sustained?
**Key Topics:** Mercantilism, British Raj, Two-Power Standard, Ironclad, Captive Market, East India Company (EIC), Sepoy Mutiny, Naval Supremacy

topics.title: 5. How did the Empire strike back? The 1857 Indian Rebellion
points: **Objective:** To understand How did the Empire strike back? The 1857 Indian Rebellion
**Key Topics:** Sepoy, Doctrine of Lapse, British Raj, Mutiny, East India Company (EIC), Rani Lakshmibai

topics.title: 6. How did ordinary people fight for a voice?
points: **Objective:** To understand How did ordinary people fight for a voice?
**Key Topics:** Franchise, Chartism, Swing Riots, Constitutional Reform, Transportation, Peterloo Massacre, Tolpuddle Martyrs, People's Charter

topics.title: 7. How did the road to democracy expand?
points: **Objective:** To understand How did the road to democracy expand?
**Key Topics:** Rotten Borough, Pocket Borough, Franchise, Constituency, Secret Ballot, Great Reform Act 1832, Hustings, Benjamin Disraeli

topics.title: 8. Who truly benefited from 19th-century transformation?
points: **Objective:** To understand Who truly benefited from 19th-century transformation?
**Key Topics:** Synthesis, Historiographical Debate, Façade, Oligarchy, Concession
